title: Enforce table level access control on data lake tables using AWS Glue 5.0 with AWS Lake Formation
key_points: Glue 5.0 adds full-table access: if a job role has all-table Lake Formation permission, plain Spark (DataFrames, SQL, RDDs, UDFs, MERGE) can read and write Hive and Iceberg tables under Lake Formation.
Fine-grained access (rows, columns, cells) is still available but restricts which Spark features work.
Shows migrating a Glue 4.0 GlueContext-based job to native Spark with full-table access.
services: AWS Glue, AWS Lake Formation, Apache Iceberg
decision: Full-table vs fine-grained Lake Formation enforcement for Glue Spark jobs
authors: Layth Yassin, Matt Su, Kartik Panjabi, Noritaka Sekiyama

title: Amazon Redshift Python user-defined functions will reach end of support after June 30, 2026
key_points: Redshift stopped allowing new Python UDFs and suspended existing ones after 30 June 2026; the replacement is Lambda UDFs called from SQL.
Walkthrough finds existing Python UDFs, rewrites one as a Lambda, registers it and swaps it in; a Kiro skill is offered for bulk conversion, plus cost and monitoring guidance.
Lambda UDFs bring current Python runtimes, outside API calls and separate scaling, at the price of per-call latency and Lambda cost.
services: Amazon Redshift, AWS Lambda, Kiro
decision: Rewrite UDF logic in SQL vs move it to Lambda UDFs vs move it out of the warehouse into the pipeline
authors: Raks Khare, Harshida Patel, Ritesh Sinha, Yanzhu Ji

title: Introducing AWS Glue Data Catalog usage metrics for API usage
key_points: Glue Data Catalog API calls now appear as CloudWatch usage metrics at minute-level granularity across many API operations.
Use them to spot quota pressure early, enable anomaly detection and alarm on unusual catalog traffic from engines or crawlers.
Small launch, mostly a console walkthrough.
services: AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon CloudWatch
decision: Watch catalog API usage vs wait for throttling errors in jobs
authors: David Zhang, Abhay Joshi, Sandeep Adwankar, Noritaka Sekiyama

title: Enhance data ingestion performance in Amazon Redshift with concurrent inserts
key_points: Concurrent INSERT and COPY statements into the same Redshift table used to run strictly one after another; now their scan, sort and aggregate phases run in parallel and only the final write is serialised.

Removes the old workaround of per-loader staging tables plus ALTER TABLE APPEND, and also helps multi-warehouse writes through data sharing; AWS reports up to 40% shorter end-to-end time for scan-heavy loads.
Deadlock risk: a transaction that inserts and then updates, merges, deletes or runs DDL on the same table should be split.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift data sharing
decision: Concurrent loads into one table vs staging tables with ALTER TABLE APPEND for parallel ingestion
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (parallel model loads on Redshift Serverless)
authors: Raghu Kuppala, Gagan Goel, Kshitij Batra, Sanuj Basu, Sumant Nemmani

title: Building serverless event streaming applications with Amazon MSK and AWS Lambda
key_points: Lambda can consume Kafka topics on MSK through an event source mapping, so no consumer group code or compute fleet is needed; the walkthrough includes a cross-account setup.

Tuning levers: provisioned mode for the pollers (sized from throughput; capped at the partition count to keep order), batch size and batching window, filters to skip irrelevant records, provisioned concurrency for latency.
The same levers carry over to Lambda consumers on Kinesis.
services: AWS Lambda, Amazon MSK
decision: Lambda event source mapping vs self-managed consumer apps (containers, Flink) for per-record Kafka processing
authors: Tarun Rai Madan, Masudur Rahaman Sayem

key_points: Fluent Bit running outside AWS gets short-lived credentials from IAM Roles Anywhere and signs its log uploads to OpenSearch Ingestion, so no long-term keys are stored.
Log-platform security pattern, off the reader's path.

title: Capture data lineage from dbt, Apache Airflow, and Apache Spark with Amazon SageMaker
key_points: A small proxy (API Gateway, SQS, Lambda) receives OpenLineage events and posts them to the SageMaker Catalog / DataZone lineage API.
Shows the OpenLineage settings for dbt, Airflow and Glue 4.0 Spark so their runs appear in one lineage graph next to natively captured Glue and Redshift lineage.
Glue 5.0 sends OpenLineage natively; later posts cover lineage for more sources.

decision: dbt's own docs lineage vs a central catalog fed by OpenLineage events from every tool

title: How Skroutz handles real-time schema evolution in Amazon Redshift with Debezium
key_points: Skroutz streams MariaDB and MongoDB changes through Debezium and Kafka into Redshift, and never lets a new source column break the load: unknown fields go into a catch-all SUPER column as JSON.
A weekly check lists tables with data in that column; engineers then add the real column, update the consumer and loader, and move the parked values across.
Production tables use slowly changing dimension Type 7 with a staging-then-promote load.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift SUPER / PartiQL, Debezium, Apache Kafka
aws_type: Customer Solutions / Experience-Based Acceleration / Technical How-to · 300
decision: Fail on schema drift vs auto-add columns vs park unknown fields in a SUPER column for later promotion in CDC loads

title: Build a multi-Region analytics solution with Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, and AWS Quick Sight
key_points: Keeps regulated data stored in its home Region's Redshift while a global analytics Region reads it through cross-Region data sharing and serves Quick Sight dashboards.
Covers cross-Region networking for Quick Sight, and the latency, security and transfer-cost trade-offs.
Notes the design addresses where data is stored, not whether it crosses Regions in transit.

title: RocksDB 101: Optimizing stateful streaming in Apache Spark with Amazon EMR and AWS Glue
key_points: For Spark Structured Streaming jobs with large state (aggregations, de-duplication), the RocksDB state store keeps state off the JVM heap, cutting garbage-collection pressure, and checkpoints fewer, larger files to S3.

Off-heap memory still counts against the container, so raise memory overhead; tune write buffers and block cache, turn on changelog checkpointing (EMR 7.0+, Glue 5.0) and keep fewer old state versions.
Watch local disk: compact on commit, and on Glue use G.2X or larger workers.
services: AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Apache Spark, RocksDB
decision: Default in-memory state store vs RocksDB for stateful Spark streaming on Glue or EMR
authors: Melody Yang, Dai Ozaki, Noritaka Sekiyama, Amir Shenavandeh, Xi Yang

title: Reduce time to access your transactional data for analytical processing using the power of Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse and zero-ETL
key_points: Aurora MySQL replicates into Redshift Serverless through zero-ETL; the Redshift namespace is then registered in the lakehouse catalog so the same data is reachable through Iceberg APIs.
Lake Formation adds fine-grained permissions and analysts query it from SageMaker Unified Studio; set-up comes as a CloudFormation stack.
Shows one copy of operational data serving both SQL analytics and Iceberg-compatible engines.
services: zero-ETL (Aurora MySQL to Redshift), Amazon Redshift Serverless, Amazon Aurora MySQL, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio

title: How Nexthink built real-time alerts with Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
key_points: Nexthink, a heavy Kafka Streams user on MSK, picked Flink for real-time alerting because Kafka Streams ties parallelism to partition counts, needs co-partitioned topics for joins and puts state load on Kafka.
Flink jobs compute seasonal baselines and evaluate threshold rules over sliding windows, joined with alert configuration streamed from a topic.
Lessons: Flink state is hard to inspect, and watermarks need careful tuning when joining streams that run at different speeds or go idle.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Amazon MSK, Kafka Streams, Amazon EKS
decision: Kafka Streams in microservices vs a separate Flink job for stateful, event-time stream processing
